title: React Module 02 Applied Check
description: Apply component, prop, state, children, and composition concepts to realistic React design choices and mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A `Card` component should wrap arbitrary headings, paragraphs, and buttons. Which API is most flexible?

options.text: Accept `children` and render it inside the card
Use one global variable named content

questions.explanation: `children` lets layout components wrap arbitrary JSX supplied by the parent.

questions.prompt: A child needs to request that a parent updates selected item state. Which are appropriate? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Call the callback from the child event handler
Mutate the parent state variable directly from the child
Keep the source of truth in the common parent

questions.explanation: Parents own state; children communicate through callback props.

questions.prompt:
What is wrong with `function User({ user }) { user.name = "New"; return

{user.name}

; }`?

options.text: It mutates a prop during render

questions.explanation: Components should treat props as immutable and avoid side effects during render.

questions.prompt: A prop is optional and should default to `"Button"`. Which pattern is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Default values can be supplied through JavaScript parameter defaults when destructuring props.

questions.prompt: Passing a new inline function as a prop is always a bug in beginner React apps.
questions.explanation: Function props are common for events. Identity can matter for optimization later, but inline callbacks are not automatically bugs.

questions.prompt: Two sibling components must show and change the same selected value. Where should the state usually live?
questions.explanation: Shared state should be lifted to the closest owner that can pass values and callbacks down.

questions.prompt: Which are signs that a component may be doing too much? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It mixes unrelated layout, data rules, and many event flows
It cannot be reused without copying large blocks
It has a clear name and one focused responsibility
Small changes regularly break unrelated UI inside it

questions.explanation: Focused components are easier to reuse and maintain; unrelated responsibilities make them fragile.
Nested JSX becomes the `children` prop of the wrapping component.
